sentences.text: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized ankylosaurine that reached a total length of 5 meters when fully grown.
This dinosaur weighed up to 1.9 metric tons.
The maxilla of the animal bears about fourteen teeth.
The upper snout armor consists of a fused mass rather than distinct scales called caputegulae.
Pinacosaurus has between two and five additional openings near the nostrils, the purpose of which remains unexplained.
A group of juvenile Pinacosaurus found at Bayan Mandahu were all oriented in the same direction, suggesting they were a traveling herd killed and buried by a sandstorm.
Juvenile Pinacosaurus found in groups were all approximately the same age, with an average length of about 1.5 meters.
The structure of Pinacosaurus's tongue and teeth might suggest it exhibited ant-eater-like insectivorous behavior.
The American Museum of Natural History sponsored Central Asiatic Expeditions to the Gobi Desert in Mongolia during the 1920s.
Yang Zhongjian described the species Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis in 1935 based on a specimen from the Bayan Mandahu Formation in Ningxia Province.
The genus Pinacosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1933.
In 2014, Arbour established some distinctive traits of the genus Pinacosaurus.
New fossil material of Pinacosaurus grangeri was described by Zhu et al. in 2026 from the Upper Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation in China.
Juvenile Pinacosaurus possessed large tongue bones showing signs of muscular stress, suggesting they relied heavily on muscular tongues for feeding.
Pinacosaurus likely had a varied diet that included tough leaves and pulpy fruits, though it probably avoided fibrous and woody plants.
Pinacosaurus had rows of small, weak teeth inside its mouth that influenced its diet.
Pinacosaurus likely avoided hard stems and pine needles, instead ingesting soft, low-growing ferns that were easy to cut.
During growth, juvenile Pinacosaurus developed fused ribs and increasingly robust forelimbs, indicating that their arms bore most of their body weight.
A fossilized larynx was described from a juvenile Pinacosaurus specimen by Yoshida et al. in 2023.
The structure of the Pinacosaurus larynx suggests it was capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations.
Researchers suggest Pinacosaurus had a relatively light build to gain agility for fighting small theropods, using its club to hit swift targets.
Like other ankylosaurs, Pinacosaurus had a thick club at the end of its tail used as a defensive weapon against large predators.
The strong development of the hyoid suggests that a powerful tongue compensated for weakly developed dentition.
Originally classified in Nodosauridae by Gilmore, Pinacosaurus is now considered an ankylosaurid and likely a member of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
Synonyms for Pinacosaurus include Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis, Heishansaurus pachycephalus, and Syrmosaurus viminocaudus.
Pinacosaurus belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae.
Pinacosaurus lived in Mongolia and China during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
Pinacosaurus lived in a semi-desert habitat interspersed with oases.
In 2015, Arbour and Currie concluded that Heishansaurus pachycephalus was a nomen dubium.
Robert Hill argued in 2012 that P. mephistocephalus was a valid species based on its secondary dermal horns and narial characteristics.
It has been suggested that some additional holes are the result of damage.
Maryańska in 1977 thought the structure was a tabular bone unknown in dinosaurs, suggesting Ankylosauria evolved independently of Aetosauria, a hypothesis now completely discarded.
